reconstruction: Several Holby City' origins spin-offs. Casualty and Holby City closely share the same premises and some characters have appeared in both programmes, and screened an occasional crossover mini-drama entitled Casualty @ Holby City, with shared casts. Crossovers also occur, occasionally with self-contained storylines; developing romantic relationships between Holby City's Nick Jordan and Casualty's Linda Andrews, Holby City's Ric Griffin and Casualty's Guppy Sandhu and Holby City's Elliot Hope and Casualty's Ruth Winters. The crossover storylines were often spearheaded by Casualty's Executive Producer Mervyn Watson, and Holby City's Executive Producer Tony McHale. Logistical reasons prevented the show running for more than 120 episodes, which production was halted. However, a special one-off episode was commissioned in 2005, titled "Casualty@Holby City", aiming to promote organ donation and highlighting the shortage of organ donors in the UK. In order to generate interactive content for the show, the BBC produced a fictional website featuring patient information and medical resources. Casualty @ Holby City aired on Boxing Day 2005. The special two-part storyline tackled topical issues, such as the turbulent relationship between doctors and the police, and anti-war demonstrations outside the hospital. In December 2004 a crossover episode of Casualty was filmed for broadcast in 2005. In order to maintain the separation of the two filming crews, each part of the crossover was specifically operated by a different crew, with Paul Unwin and Simon Mirren producing the Casualty episodes and Richard Harrison producing the Holby City episodes.

reference: In Oedipus the King , Oedipus is the protagonist . Oedipus ' infanticide is planned by his parents , Laius and Jocasta , to avert him from fulfilling a prophecy ; in truth , the servant entrusted with the infanticide passes the infant on through a series of intermediaries to a childless couple , who adopt him not knowing his history . Oedipus eventually learns of the Delphic Oracle 's prophecy of him , that he would kill his father and marry his mother ; Oedipus attempts to flee his fate without harming those he knows as his parents ( at this point , he does not know that he is adopted ) . Oedipus meets a man at a crossroads accompanied by servants ; Oedipus and the man fought , and Oedipus killed the man . ( This man was his father , Laius , not that anyone apart from the gods knew this at the time ) . He becomes the ruler of Thebes after solving the riddle of the sphinx and in the process , marries the widowed queen , his mother Jocasta . Thus the stage is set for horror . When the truth comes out , following from another true but confusing prophecy from Delphi , Jocasta commits suicide , Oedipus blinds himself and leaves Thebes . At the end of the play , order is restored . This restoration is seen when Creon , brother of Jocasta , becomes king , and also when Oedipus , before going off to exile , asks Creon to take care of his children . Oedipus 's children will always bear the weight of shame and humiliation because of their father 's actions .

reference: On 31 August 1937 , three Hawker Demon aircraft of No. 1 Squadron were on a training flight , during which they landed at an air base in Hamilton , Victoria . The exercise coincided with the local agricultural show , and the planes briefly provided a stationary display for the public . Recommencing their journey , the first aircraft had already taken off when the second was seen to have difficulties . The pilot , Pilot Officer Kenneth McKenzie , had attempted a climbing turn when the aircraft 's engine stalled , sending the machine into a dive . McAloney — who was a passenger in the third aircraft — witnessed the incident and signalled for his pilot to stop . On doing this , McAloney immediately leapt out of his plane and ran across the airfield . Out of control , the second aircraft struck the ground and rapidly became engulfed in flames . The first on scene , McAloney dashed into the wreckage in an effort to extradite the two crew members , and was able to grab hold of McKenzie who was sprawled over the flaming main fuel tank . McAloney pulled McKenzie free of the cockpit and down on to the aircraft 's wing , though McKenzie 's leg became trapped in the wreckage . Despite this , McAloney continued his efforts to free McKenzie , burning his hands on the pilot 's smouldering clothes . At this point , one of the wing tanks burst , rendering McAloney unconscious . He was pulled from the aircraft suffering severe burns , and spent the next four weeks in hospital undergoing treatment . Both McKenzie and his observer @-@ gunner , Sergeant Norman Torrens @-@ Witherow , perished and it was later ascertained that , owing to the injuries sustained on impact , they would not have survived even if the rescue attempt had been successful .

reference: The son of Tughj ibn Juff , a general of Transoxianian origin who served both the Abbasids and the autonomous Tulunid rulers of Egypt and Syria , Muhammad ibn Tughj was born in Baghdad but grew up in Syria and acquired his first military and administrative experiences at his father 's side . He had a turbulent early career : he was imprisoned along with his father by the Abbasids in 905 , was released in 906 , participated in the murder of the vizier al @-@ Abbas ibn al @-@ Hasan al @-@ Jarjara 'i in 908 , and fled Iraq to enter the service of the governor of Egypt , Takin al @-@ Khazari . Eventually he acquired the patronage of several influential Abbasid magnates , chiefly the powerful commander @-@ in @-@ chief Mu 'nis al @-@ Muzaffar . These ties led him to being named governor first of Palestine and then of Damascus . In 933 , he was briefly named governor of Egypt , but this order was revoked after the death of Mu 'nis , and Ibn Tughj had to fight to preserve even his governorship of Damascus . In 935 , he was re @-@ appointed to Egypt , where he quickly defeated a Fatimid invasion and stabilized the turbulent country . His reign marks a rare period of domestic peace , stability and good government in the annals of early Islamic Egypt . reference: Placed under the command of William D. Leahy in April 1918 , the ship was readied for her first transatlantic troop run . At Newport News , Virginia , elements of the 4th Infantry Division boarded on 9 May . Sailing at 18 : 30 the next day , Princess Matoika was accompanied by American transports Pastores , Wilhelmina , Lenape , Antigone , and Susquehanna , the British steamer Kursk , and the Italian Duca d 'Aosta . The group rendezvoused with a similar group that left New York the same day , consisting of President Lincoln , Covington , Rijndam , British troopship Dwinsk , and Italian steamers Caserta and Dante Alighieri . American cruiser Frederick served as escort for the assembled ships , which were the 35th U.S. convoy of the war . During the voyage — because of the inability to finish serving three meals for all the men during daylight hours — mess service was curtailed to two daily meals , a practice continued on later voyages . On 20 May , the convoy sighted and fired on a " submarine " that turned out to be a bucket ; the next day escort Frederick left the convoy after being relieved by nine destroyers . Three days later the convoy sighted land at 06 : 30 and anchored at Brest that afternoon . Princess Matoika sailed for Newport News and arrived there safely on 6 June with Pastores and Lenape . Fate , however , was not as kind to former convoy mates President Lincoln and Dwinsk . On their return journeys they were sunk by German submarines U @-@ 90 and U @-@ 151 , respectively .

reference: In the middle of December , twin monsoon troughs were established in the extreme western Pacific Ocean , which will later spawn storms Greg , and Fern itself in the northern hemisphere . The trough in the southern hemisphere spawned cyclones Ophelia , Phil , and Fergus . Around that time , convection began to increase near the equator , and was associated with a westerly wind burst . A low level circulation center was noted by JTWC on December 19 at 0600 UTC . Two days later , convection consolidated near the circulation center , and JMA began tracking it at 0000 UTC as a tropical depression . JTWC issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert at 1500 UTC , as sea level pressure began to deepen , and signs of upper level divergence were found in the system . The first advisory for Tropical Depression 42W followed three hours later , on December 17 at 1200 UTC . JTWC upgraded the depression to a tropical storm on December 22 at 0000 UTC as it traveled westerly , and was given the name Fern . According to JTWC , the wind speeds meandered at minimal tropical storm strength . JMA proceeded to upgrade the depression into a tropical storm at 1800 UTC , with winds of 65 km / h ( 40 mph ) , and a pressure reading of 996 hectopascals ( 996 mbar ) . On Christmas Eve , Fern slowly traveled toward Yap . The storm passed over Yap the next day , strengthening to 105 km / h ( 65 mph ) at 0000 UTC , according to JTWC . JMA assessed Fern had winds of 100 km / h ( 60 mph ) at the same time . Fern also began its recurvature that day , beginning its turn north .

Baldry enjoyed his greatest success with pop ballads , beginning with " Let the Heartaches Begin " ( 1967 ) , which reached number one in Britain , but , despite supporting the Beatles and the Rolling Stones , he remained virtually unknown outside of the UK . reference: The 4 × 100 m medley relay was the focal point of Tonelli 's Moscow campaign . The event had always been won by the United States since its inception at the Olympics at the 1960 Games , and their boycott had opened up the field . Australia 's best result had come in the inaugural race , when it out @-@ touched Japan to claim silver . The only other time that it had won a medal was in 1964 , taking bronze , and the previous outing in 1976 had seen Australia eliminated in the heats . Australia was regarded as a chance of a medal , but were not seen as the main threats , with Sweden , Great Britain and the Soviet Union the most heavily fancied teams . The hosts ' team included the silver medallists in the 100 m backstroke and breaststroke , and their butterflyer had come fifth ; their freestyler would come fourth in his event . The British boasted Duncan Goodhew , the breaststroke gold medallist , while Sweden 's butterflyer and backstroker had won their respective events and their freestyle swimmer would come second in the 100 m . On paper , Australia 's team paled in comparison . Neil Brooks , the freestyler , would come fourteenth in the corresponding individual event after having an asthma attack , while Peter Evans was the only individual medallist in the distance , claiming bronze in the 100 m breaststroke . Kerry had been eliminated in the backstroke semifinals , while Tonelli was swimming as a makeshift butterflyer . Adding to the pressure was the fact that Australia won no gold medals at the 1976 Olympics in any sport , so the public were still awaiting their first victory since the 1972 Games in Munich . Coming into the Olympics , Australia were ranked seventh out of the thirteen competing countries .

reference: Prithvi Kumar Agrawala has traced at least six different lists of fifty or more aspects or forms of Ganesha each with their specific female consorts or shaktis . In these lists of paired shaktis are found such goddess names as Hrī , Śrī , Puṣṭī , etc . The names Buddhi , Siddhi , and Riddhi do not appear on any of these lists . The lists provide no details about the personalities or distinguishing iconographic forms for these shaktis . Agrawala concludes that all of the lists were derived from one original set of names . The earliest of the lists appears in the Nārada Purāṇa ( I.66.124 @-@ 38 ) , and appears to have been used with minor variations in the Ucchiṣṭagaṇapati Upāsanā . These lists are of two types . In the first type the names of various forms of Ganesha are given with a clear @-@ cut pairing of a named shakti for that form . The second type , as found in the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa ( II.IV.44.63 – 76 ) and the commentary of Rāghavabhaṭṭa on the Śāradātilaka ( I.115 ) , gives fifty or more names of Ganesha collectively in one group , with the names of the shaktis provided collectively in a second group . The second type of list poses problems in separating and properly connecting the names into pairs due to ambiguities in the formation of Sanskrit compound words .

reference: As the first four matches of the series were drawn , the final Test , played at The Oval , was decisive . Aware that England had beaten Australia only once in 19 matches , the selectors made several changes to the team ; Chapman , at the time fourth in the national batting averages , replaced Carr as captain . This decision was controversial ; the press favoured Carr , particularly as Chapman was young , unproven as captain and not fully established in the team . When the match began on 14 August , Chapman won the toss and decided that England should bat first . When it was his turn to bat , he was given a good reception by the crowd . During his innings , Wisden noted , Chapman " hit out in vigorous fashion " , but once he was dismissed for 49 , the remaining batsmen were out quickly , leaving England with a disappointing total of 280 . Australia replied with 302 . On a pitch affected by rain , England then scored 436 , mainly because of a large partnership between opening batsmen Jack Hobbs and Herbert Sutcliffe . Australia needed to score 415 to win , which was unlikely given the condition of the pitch . The team were bowled out for 125 , and at least one of Chapman 's tactical decisions resulted in Australia losing a wicket . Wisden reported that " not a catch was missed nor was a run given away , the whole England side rising gallantly to the occasion . Naturally a scene of tremendous enthusiasm occurred at the end , the crowd swarming in thousands in front of the pavilion , and loudly cheering the players , both English and Australian . " The correspondent also commented " Chapman ... despite lack of experience in leading a first @-@ class team in the field , turned out a very happy nomination for the post of captain , the young amateur , for the most part , managing his bowling with excellent judgement , and in two or three things he did , showing distinct imagination . " Throughout the match , Chapman chose to follow his own tactics rather than rely on the veteran players in the team for advice . In the series , he scored 175 runs at 58 @.@ 33 .

The deputy ( member ) of the People 's Council acts on the behalf of the people , and has the right to make proposals to the People 's Council and other local State organs . Ellet planned to use this system as a basket ferry to shuttle workers and materials across the gorge , saving time that would otherwise have been spent on land and ferry travel . Through media coverage and word @-@ of @-@ mouth , many people knew of Ellet 's efforts and flocked to the site to watch the construction . On March 13 , 1848 , the system was completed , and the team planned to test it by pulling the empty basket across . They hit a snag when the basket kept getting stuck halfway and could not move ahead . Pulling back the basket , Ellet decided to assure the watching crowd that the system was workable . He stepped into the basket , and it moved towards the opposite shore . When Ellet reached the problematic spot , he spotted the issue ; the basket 's rollers could not pass over a portion of the cable that had been accidentally flattened during the construction . He fixed the problem and proceeded to cross to the Canadian side and back , becoming the first person to cross the gorge . Although the bridge companies had prohibited Ellet from collecting tolls , he charged each person $ 1 @.@ 00 for the chance to " observe first hand the engineering wonder of bridging the Niagara " . This event was 'problematic' for the dam: as the river flattened the area upstream of the dam, an island of trees and debris began to float towards the dam. This mass of debris was approximately 1,000 feet (300 m) wide and 10 feet (3 m) deep. The dam was not designed to handle such a large object, and there was concern that the debris could clog the dam's spillway, causing the dam to be overtopped.

At 3:05 a.m., the river crested over the auxiliary spillway of the dam, which was designed to handle such events. The river eroded the earthen spillway at an accelerated rate, as the soil consisted of easily eroded sandy material. The main concrete spillway was designed to handle flows of up to 114,000 cubic feet per second (3,200 m3/s), but at 8:05 a.m., it was estimated that the flow rate was 163,000 cu ft/s (4,600 m3/s), and increasing. At 8:40 a.m., the auxiliary spillway collapsed, and the river was flowing through the resulting 750-foot (230 m) gap at a rate of 650,000 cu ft/s (18,000 m3/s).

The collapse of the auxiliary spillway removed support for the main concrete spillway and the dam itself. At 9:00 a.m., the dam suffered a catastrophic failure and collapsed. Within hours, a large portion of the reservoir was emptied. Only a small pool remained behind the dam.

Aftermath

The sudden release of water sent a wave of debris, trees, and water down the valley of the West Fork River, destroying all in its path. The towns of Rapid City and Keystone were the hardest hit, as they were located in the narrow valley below the dam. The floodwaters reached Rapid City around 11:00 p.m., reaching a height of 12 feet (3.7 m) in some areas. The floodwaters destroyed homes, businesses, and infrastructure. Over 1,335 homes were completely destroyed, and another 1,788 were heavily damaged. Hundreds of businesses were destroyed as well.

At the 1972 elections the Pangu Pati, as it was then known, gained 621 more votes than its nearest rival, and won 18 of the 81 seats. Michael Somare became Chief Minister, with John Guise as Deputy Chief Minister, and Ebia Olewale as Minister for Education. Albert Maori Kiki became Minister for Defence, Information and Culture, and Donatus Mola was made Minister for Agriculture. In 1973, Somare outlined eight aims for his government, including rural improvement, equal distribution of resources, decentralisation of economic activity, and government control of the economy. On 16 September 1975, Papua New Guinea gained independence, and Somare became the country's first Prime Minister. He was knighted in 1991.
After independence, the Pangu Party continued to play a significant role in PNG politics, either as part of the government or in opposition. In the years following independence, there was no dominant political party, and governments were formed through coalition. The Pangu Party became the largest party in the National Parliament at the 1977 elections, but Somare was not able to form a majority government. In 1980, a vote of no confidence brought down Somare's government, and Sir Julius Chan became Prime Minister.
Pangu returned to power in 1982, and Somare again became Prime Minister. His government was defeated in 1985, and Paias Wingti became Prime Minister. Pangu returned to power again in 1988, with Rabbie Namaliu as Prime Minister. The party lost power in 1992, and was in opposition until 1999, when it became part of a coalition government, with Sir Mekere Morauta as Prime Minister. In 2002, Pangu returned to opposition, but in 2007 became part of a coalition led by Prime Minister Sir Michael Somare.
As of 2007, the Pangu Party was led by Chris Haiveta. At the 2007 election, Pangu won 3 seats. In 2010, it was led by Andrew Kumbakor.
In March 2017, Sam Basil left the Pangu Party with other MPs to form a new party, the People's United Resource Party. Soon after, businessman Brian Kramer was appointed as the party leader and led the party into the 2017 general elections, and subsequently led successful negotiations which resulted in the party becoming part of the coalition government led by Prime Minister Peter O'Neill, with Kramer appointed as Minister of Police.
In May 2019, Kramer resigned from the O'Neill government and crossed the floor with his Pangu Party MPs to join the opposition, subsequently supporting James Marape in his successful challenge to become Prime Minister. Kramer became Minister of Police again in the Marape government.
In June 2019, the Pangu Party declared that it was reviving Somare's original vision, and that its policies were consistent with Somare's "Gamabada" policies. The party's candidates for the 2022 general election would be selected on this basis.
On 24 August 2020, the Pangu Party appointed incumbent Prime Minister James Marape as its party leader. Marape led the party into the 2022 general election, where it won 39 seats, the most of any party.

reconstruction: Hurricane Dora was a powerful Category 4 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 929 mbar ( hPa; 27.44 inHg). Dora formed on July 12 and dissipated on August 19. Dora, along with Hurricane Eugene, caused heavy surf along the coast of California. The remnant moisture from Dora contributed to rainfall in Arizona. , which helped relieve the extreme heatwave the state was experiencing. Dora crossed into the Western Pacific on July 31, becoming the first tropical cyclone to do so as a hurricane since 2018. Dora moved into the Western Pacific with winds of 140 mph (220 km/h) as it crossed the dateline at 9°N, and continued to gradually weaken. The storm was located about 1,675 miles (2,700 km) east-southeast of Tokyo, Japan. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) continued to track Dora as a tropical cyclone, and gave it the international designation 2308 and the PAGASA name Goring, though it was no longer considered a tropical cyclone by the JTWC. Dora weakened to a tropical storm on August 4 and transitioned into a remnant low on August 7. The remnant low of Dora dissipated entirely on August 12. Dora was the fifth hurricane of the 2023 Pacific hurricane season. Dora was named after Paul Douglas, who worked as a meteorologist. Hurricane Dora caused $35,000,000 (2023 USD) in damage.

reference: Businessman Clifford Coombs took over as chairman in 1965 , luring Stan Cullis out of retirement to manage the club . Cullis 's team played attractive football which took them to the semifinals of the League Cup in 1967 and the FA Cup in 1968 , but league football needed a different approach . Successor Freddie Goodwin produced a team playing skilful , aggressive football that won promotion as well as reaching an FA Cup semifinal . Two years later , the club raised money by selling Bob Latchford to Everton for a British record fee of £ 350 @,@ 000 , but without his goals the team struggled . Sir Alf Ramsey briefly managed the club before Jim Smith took over in 1978 . With relegation a certainty , the club sold Trevor Francis to Nottingham Forest , making him the first player transferred for a fee of £ 1 million ; Francis had scored a total of 133 goals in 329 appearances over his nine years at Birmingham . Smith took Birmingham straight back to the First Division , but a poor start to the 1981 – 82 season saw him replaced by Ron Saunders , who had just resigned from league champions Aston Villa . Saunders ' team struggled to score goals and in 1984 they were relegated . They bounced back up , but the last home game of the 1984 – 85 promotion season , against Leeds United , was marred by rioting , culminating in the death of a boy when a wall collapsed on him . "A Song for You" is a song written by Leon Russell in 1970. It was first recorded by Russell and appeared on his self-titled debut album. A wide range of artists have recorded versions of the song, including Donny Hathaway, Helen Reddy, Andy Williams, The Carpenters, Willie Nelson, Ray Charles, Peggy Lee, and Whitney Houston.

In 2021, the song was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

Stafford Braxton Thomas (born October 25, 1975), better known as "Braxton", is an American multi-platinum songwriter and producer. He has written and produced songs for artists such as Toni Braxton, Kelly Rowland, Jill Scott, Pharrell Williams, Solange Knowles, Ariana Grande, Justin Bieber, and Usher.

Thomas got his start in the music industry as a teenager, working with Rodney Jerkins and LaShawn Daniels. He later signed a publishing deal with EMI Music Publishing.

Thomas has won several awards throughout his career, including a Grammy Award for Best R&B Album for Toni Braxton's "Love & War". He has also been nominated for several other Grammy Awards, including Songwriter of the Year.

In addition to his work as a songwriter and producer, Thomas is also a mentor to young musicians. He has worked with several organizations to help aspiring artists develop their talents.

Locke & Key is an American fantasy horror drama television series developed by Carlton Cuse, Meredith Averill, and Aron Eli Coleite, based on the comic-book series of the same name by Joe Hill and Gabriel Rodríguez. It premiered on Netflix on February 7, 2020.

The series revolves around the Locke family—siblings Tyler, Kinsey, and Bode—who, after the murder of their father, move from Seattle to their ancestral home in Matheson, Massachusetts, known as Keyhouse. They soon discover that the house is full of magical keys that can unlock various doors in the house and grant them various powers. However, they are also being hunted by a demonic entity who wants the keys for her own nefarious purposes.

The series stars Darby Stanchfield, Connor Jessup, Emilia Jones, Jackson Robert Scott, Laysla De Oliveira, Petrice Jones, Griffin Gluck, and Hallea Jones.

The first season of Locke & Key received mixed reviews from critics. While some praised the show's cast and visuals, others criticized its writing and pacing. The second season, which premiered on October 22, 2021, received more positive reviews. The third and final season was released on August 10, 2022.

Flashback (stylized as FLASHBACK) is a 2021 Canadian psychological thriller film directed by Christopher MacBride and starring Dylan O'Brien, Hannah Gross, Emory Cohen, and Keir Gilchrist.

The film follows Fred Fitzell (O'Brien), a man who begins to have disturbing flashbacks to his teenage years, leading him to question his sanity and the reality of his life.

Flashback premiered at the Sitges Film Festival on October 9, 2020, and was released in the United States on June 4, 2021.

TMZ is an American tabloid news website. It launched on November 8, 2005, and is operated by Fox Entertainment. It features celebrity news, gossip, and videos. The name TMZ stands for "Thirty Mile Zone", a reference to the historic "studio zone" within a 30-mile radius of Hollywood defined in the collective bargaining agreements between the studios and unions.

Graded Readers are books written for language learners. They are written with a limited vocabulary and grammar, and are often shorter than original works of literature. Graded readers are designed to help learners improve their reading skills and vocabulary.

The semicolon (;) is a punctuation mark that separates two independent clauses that are closely related in thought. It can also be used to separate items in a list when those items contain commas.

Forward slash (/) is a punctuation mark that is used to separate words or phrases. It is also used in fractions and dates.

Unconventional warfare (UW) is the support of a resistance movement or insurgency to coerce, disrupt or overthrow a government or occupying power.

Ralph Waldo Emerson (May 25, 1803 – April 27, 1882) was an American essayist, lecturer, philosopher, abolitionist and poet who led the transcendentalist movement of the mid-19th century. He was seen as a champion of individualism and a prescient critic of the countervailing pressures of society, and he disseminated his thoughts through dozens of published essays and more than 1,500 public lectures across the United States.

Arianna Huffington (born Ariadna Stassinopoulos; July 15, 1950) is a Greek-American author, syndicated columnist, and businesswoman. She is a co-founder of The Huffington Post, and the founder and CEO of Thrive Global.

Huffington was born in Athens, Greece. She moved to the United Kingdom at age 16 and studied economics at Girton College, Cambridge.

Huffington began her career as a writer and commentator. She has written several books, including biographies of Maria Callas and Pablo Picasso.

Huffington co-founded The Huffington Post in 2005. The website quickly became one of the most popular news and opinion websites in the world.

In 2016, Huffington left The Huffington Post to launch Thrive Global, a company that focuses on health and wellness.

Sarajevo 's population in 1991 , according to that census , was 525,980 . During the Bosnian War , from 1992 to 1995 , the city suffered a prolonged siege . The Serbian Republic was created within Bosnia and Herzegovina and its leadership wanted to include Sarajevo . From 1992 to 1995 , Sarajevo was besieged by the Army of Republika Srpska ( VRS ) and the Yugoslav People's Army ( JNA ) . The siege lasted 1,425 days , and resulted in the deaths of 11,541 people , including over 5,000 civilians . An additional 56,000 people were wounded , and much of the city was destroyed . After the war , the population dropped dramatically .

In 2002 , the population was estimated to be around 400,000 . The 2013 census recorded a population of 275,524 in the four municipalities that constitute the city of Sarajevo : Centar , Novi Grad , Novo Sarajevo , and Stari Grad . Sarajevo Canton had a population of 438,443 in 2013 .

As of 2022 , the estimated population of Sarajevo is around 343,000 . The majority of the population are Bosniaks . Other ethnic groups include Serbs , Croats , and others .

After the end of the Bosnian War , there have been efforts to rebuild and reconstruct Sarajevo . The city has undergone significant modernization , and its economy has recovered . Sarajevo is once again a major cultural and economic center in the region .

reference: The tactical decision that precedes almost every play in a baseball game involves pitch selection . By gripping and then releasing the baseball in a certain manner , and by throwing it at a certain speed , pitchers can cause the baseball to break to either side , or downward , as it approaches the batter . Among the resulting wide variety of pitches that may be thrown , the four basic types are the fastball , the changeup ( or off @-@ speed pitch ) , and two breaking balls — the curveball and the slider . Pitchers have different repertoires of pitches they are skillful at throwing . Conventionally , before each pitch , the catcher signals the pitcher what type of pitch to throw , as well as its general vertical and / or horizontal location . If there is disagreement on the selection , the pitcher may shake off the sign and the catcher will call for a different pitch . With a runner on base and taking a lead , the pitcher may attempt a pickoff , a quick throw to a fielder covering the base to keep the runner 's lead in check or , optimally , effect a tag out . Pickoff attempts , however , are subject to rules that severely restrict the pitcher 's movements before and during the pickoff attempt . Violation of any one of these rules could result in the umpire calling a balk against the pitcher , with the result being runners on base , if any , advance one base with impunity . If an attempted stolen base is anticipated , the catcher may call for a pitchout , a ball thrown deliberately off the plate , allowing the catcher to catch it while standing and throw quickly to a base . Facing a batter with a strong tendency to hit to one side of the field , the fielding team may employ a shift , with most or all of the fielders moving to the left or right of their usual positions . With a runner on third base , the infielders may play in , moving closer to home plate to improve the odds of throwing out the runner on a ground ball , though a sharply hit grounder is more likely to carry through a drawn @-@ in infield .

tactical precedence. A gripping tag is a legal tag, even if the fielder makes an upward, downward, or sideways motion toward the runner. A balk is an illegal act by the pitcher with a runner or runners on base, entitling all runners to advance one base. A pitcher may not make a quick return, defined as throwing the ball immediately after receiving it and before the batter is reasonably set in the batter's box. A hidden ball trick is a play in which a fielder hides the ball from the runner, and then tags him out when he leaves the base.

Defensive indifference is when the defensive team concedes a base to a baserunner, usually at third base, by not attempting to retire him. Typically, this occurs late in the game when the run scored is not as important as making an out on the batter or another baserunner. The scorer shall credit a stolen base unless defensive indifference is evident.

Umpire interference occurs when an umpire hinders a runner from attempting to advance or prevents a fielder from making a play.

In Major League Baseball, a batted ball that hits an umpire is always ruled in play, as is a thrown ball that hits an umpire.

A runner is out when:

He runs more than three feet away from his baseline to avoid being tagged, unless his action is to avoid interference with a fielder fielding a batted ball. (The runner is still safe if he runs behind the fielder to avoid interfering with him.)

He intentionally interferes with a thrown ball, or obstructs a fielder attempting to make a play on a batted ball.

After acquiring legal possession of a base, he runs the bases in reverse order for the purpose of confusing the defense or making a travesty of the game.

The coach at first or third base physically assists him in running the bases.

One or more members of his team are physically assisting him from the dugout or bullpen.

He passes another runner before that runner is out.

He is touched by the ball while he is off base, unless a fielder is illegally obstructing him, or the ball is dropped and he is attempting to return to the base.

A preceding runner intentionally interferes with a fielder attempting to make a play at the plate with the obvious attempt to break up a double play. The runner is out and the batter is also out.

A runner who has reached home base is out if he leaves the game and attempts to return to the field to participate in a fight.

He fails to touch a base or bases in proper order (and an appeal is made).

He slides into a base in a way that's judged by the umpire to be dangerous or malicious.

He fails to avoid a fielder who is in the act of fielding a batted ball, if the fielder has a clear path to the ball, regardless of whether the runner is on or off the base.

On December 20, 2009, at 8:00 a.m., the Los Angeles Fire Department responded to her and Monjack's Los Angeles home, in the Hollywood Hills, after a call from her mother Sharon Murphy stating that Murphy had collapsed in a bathroom. She was pronounced dead at 10:04 a.m. at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.

It was stated that Murphy had been taking a range of over-the-counter and prescription medications, but it appeared she was trying to treat a cold or respiratory infection, and that neither of the drugs contributed to her death.

On May 23, 2010, five months after Murphy's death, Simon Monjack was found dead at the same Hollywood Hills residence. His death was determined to be from pneumonia and anemia.

In January 2011, Sharon Murphy announced that she believed toxic mold in the home was the cause of both Brittany and Simon's deaths. However, in a November 2011 report, the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health refuted this claim.

The **National Film Registry** (NFR) is the United States National Film Preservation Board's (NFPB) selection of films for preservation, which recognizes the cultural, historical, or aesthetic significance of motion pictures. The NFPB, which was created by the U.S. Congress under the National Film Preservation Act of 1988, and reauthorized in 1992, 1996, 2005, and 2008, is tasked with selecting films for the registry each year, as well as advising the Librarian of Congress on national film preservation policy. These films are not necessarily in the public domain, nor are they necessarily feature films. The registry includes newsreels, silent films, student films, experimental films, short films, music videos, outtakes, and film serials. The first film selections were made in 1989, and each year since then, 25 films have been added, resulting in 850 films being included in the registry as of 2022.

To be eligible for inclusion in the National Film Registry, a film must be "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant", and must be at least ten years old. Nominations are accepted from the public, as well as from members of the NFPB. The Librarian of Congress makes the final selection, after consulting with the NFPB and other film experts. While the NFR is not intended to be a list of the "best" American films, it is intended to represent the breadth and diversity of American film heritage.

The selection of a film for the National Film Registry does not guarantee its preservation, but it does increase the likelihood that it will be preserved. The NFPB works with film archives, studios, and other organizations to ensure that the films on the registry are preserved for future generations. The Library of Congress has a state-of-the-art audiovisual conservation center in Culpeper, Virginia, where many of the films on the registry are preserved. The NFPB also promotes public awareness of the importance of film preservation through educational programs and outreach activities.

Sìol Thorcaill was the dominant family on Lewis from the Late Middle Ages until the end of the 16th century . The Gaelic names Tormod and Torcall are derived from the Old Norse names Þórmóðr and Þórketill . Thomas noted that these names were also those of two men with Lewis connections , who are both recorded in the 13th @-@ century kings ' saga Hákonar saga Hákonarsonar . One of these men was Þórketill Þórmóðsson , who according to the saga , was slain near the Isle of Skye in about the year 1230 . Thomas proposed that this man could be a grandson of Ljótólfr . Another man who appears in the saga , Þórmóðr Þórketilson , was forced to flee Lewis , leaving behind his wife , retainers , and goods ; according to Thomas , this shows that Þórmóðr was a resident on the island . Thomas noted that Þórmóðr Þórketilson was married in about 1231 , and on the assumption that each generation could be estimated to be 30 years , Thomas gave Þórmóðr 's birth at 1201 ; his ( supposed ) father , Þórketill , at 1171 ; Þórketill 's father Þórmóðr at 1141 ; and this man 's father at 1111 . Thomas concluded that the elder Þórmóðr would have been born at about the time Ljótólfr flourished on Lewis .

reference: Piccadilly was named Portugal Street in 1663 after Catherine of Braganza , wife of Charles II . Its importance to traffic increased after an earlier road from Charing Cross to Hyde Park Corner was closed to allow the creation of Green Park in 1668 . After the Restoration of the English monarchy in 1660 , Charles II encouraged the development of Portugal Street and the area to the north ( Mayfair ) and they became fashionable residential localities . Some of the grandest mansions in London were built on the northern side of the street . Edward Hyde , 1st Earl of Clarendon and close political adviser to the king , purchased land for a house ; Clarendon House ( now the location of Albemarle Street ) was built in 1664 , and the earl sold the surplus land partly to Sir John Denham , who built what later became Burlington House . Denham chose the location because it was on the outskirts of London surrounded by fields . The house was first used to house the poor , before being reconstructed by the third Earl of Burlington in 1718 . Berkeley House was constructed around the same time as Clarendon House . It was destroyed by a fire in 1733 and rebuilt as Devonshire House in 1737 by William Cavendish , 3rd Duke of Devonshire , and was subsequently used as the headquarters for the Whig party . Devonshire House survived until 1921 , before being sold for redevelopment by Edward Cavendish , 10th Duke of Devonshire for £ 1 million . Burlington House has since been home to the Royal Academy of Arts , the Geological Society of London , the Linnean Society of London , the Royal Astronomical Society , the British Astronomical Association , the Society of Antiquaries of London and the Royal Society of Chemistry .

    Chemical peels come in light, medium, and deep formulations, each targeting a different skin depth. Deeper chemical peels offer more pronounced results but also involve longer recovery times and higher risks.
    Alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) peels are the mildest type of chemical peel and can be used at home. These peels use alpha-hydroxy acids such as glycolic acid or lactic acid to gently exfoliate the skin's surface. AHA peels can improve skin texture, reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, and even out skin tone. They are often used to treat acne and can make the skin look brighter and more radiant.
    Beta-hydroxy acid (BHA) peels are similar to AHA peels but penetrate deeper into the skin. BHA peels use beta-hydroxy acids such as salicylic acid to exfoliate the skin and unclog pores. BHA peels are particularly effective for treating acne and oily skin.
    Trichloroacetic acid (TCA) peels are a medium-depth chemical peel that can be used to treat wrinkles, sun damage, and age spots. TCA peels involve applying trichloroacetic acid to the skin, which causes the top layers of skin to peel off over the course of several days. TCA peels can produce significant results, but they also come with a higher risk of side effects such as scarring and hyperpigmentation.
    Phenol peels are the deepest type of chemical peel and are used to treat severe wrinkles, sun damage, and scars. Phenol peels involve applying phenol to the skin, which causes the top layers of skin to peel off over the course of several weeks. The X-Files is an American science fiction drama television series created by Chris Carter, which premiered on September 10, 1993, and concluded on May 19, 2002, airing for nine seasons on Fox. The series revolves around FBI special agents Fox Mulder (David Duchovny) and Dana Scully (Gillian Anderson) who are assigned to investigate X-Files: marginalized, unsolved cases involving paranormal phenomena. Mulder believes in the existence of extraterrestrials and the paranormal, while the skeptical Scully is assigned to make scientific analyses of Mulder's discoveries to debunk them, and so return him to mainstream cases. Throughout the series, both agents' lives and careers are put at risk as they uncover the government's secrets.

The X-Files is considered one of the greatest science fiction series of all time. The series introduced or further explored several themes and tropes that have since become commonplace within popular culture, including conspiracy theories, secret government agencies, and the existence of extraterrestrial life. The series popularized the concept of "monster-of-the-week" episodes, in which the protagonists investigate and resolve a self-contained paranormal case each week, while also advancing the series' overarching mythology.

The X-Files was a critical and commercial success, earning numerous awards and nominations, including 16 Primetime Emmy Awards, five Golden Globe Awards, and a Peabody Award. The series also spawned two theatrical films: The X-Files (1998) and The X-Files: I Want to Believe (2008). A revival series, consisting of six episodes, premiered on January 24, 2016, and a second revival series, consisting of ten episodes, premiered on January 3, 2018. The series has also inspired numerous books, comic books, and video games.

The show's popularity also led to the creation of a spin-off series, Millennium, which aired for three seasons from 1996 to 1999. The series followed Frank Black (Lance Henriksen), a former FBI profiler with the ability to see into the minds of criminals, as he joins the Millennium Group, a mysterious organization dedicated to fighting the forces of evil as the year 2000 approaches. Another spin-off series, The Lone Gunmen, which focused on a trio of conspiracy theorists who frequently assisted Mulder and Scully, aired for one season in 2001. The series was cancelled after 13 episodes due to low ratings.

He was disappointed that he was allowed to include so few footnotes in the original publication , and correspondingly delighted when the publishers of a German edition requested additional notes for their translation . The location of Calakmul at the edge of a bajo provided two additional advantages : the fertile soils along the edge of the swamp and access to abundant flint nodules . The first , known as the " dynamically cold " population , has orbits much like the planets ; nearly circular , with an orbital eccentricity of less than 0 @.@ 1 , and with relatively low inclinations up to about 10 ° ( they lie close to the plane of the Solar System rather than at an angle ) . The second , the " dynamically hot " population , has orbits much more inclined to the ecliptic , by up to 30 ° . Not only are the two populations in different orbits , the cold population also differs in color and albedo , being redder and brighter , has a larger fraction of binary objects , has a different size distribution , and lacks very large objects . The difference in colors may be a reflection of different compositions , which suggests they formed in different regions . The hot population is proposed to have formed near Jupiter , and to have been ejected out by movements among the giant planets . The cold population , on the other hand , has been proposed to have formed more or less in its current position . Although it has been suggested that the cold population was also swept outwards by Neptune during its migration , particularly if Neptune 's eccentricity was transiently increased , the loose binaries among the cold population are unlikely to survive encounters with Neptune during this migration . In celestial mechanics, a Trojan (or trojan) is a small celestial body (mainly an asteroid or moon) that shares the orbit of a larger planet or moon, remaining in a stable Lagrange point, specifically L4 or L5, which are located 60° ahead of and behind the larger body in its orbit. Trojans can share the orbit of a planet, but they cannot collide with it because they are gathered around one of the two Lagrangian points.

By analogy with the Trojan asteroids of Jupiter, objects at the L4 and L5 points of other planet–Sun systems are also called Trojans. In general, any small celestial body that shares the orbit of a larger one is called a Trojan. As of 2021, 12,799 Jupiter Trojans, 9 Neptune Trojans, 26 Mars Trojans, and 2 Earth Trojans have been discovered.

Origin

There are two main theories for the origin of Trojans. The "Trojan formation" theory suggests that Trojans formed in the same region as the planet they orbit, from the same protoplanetary disk material. The "capture theory" suggests that Trojans were captured from elsewhere in the Solar System, such as the Kuiper belt or the scattered disc.

Stability

The stability of Trojans is determined by a number of factors, including the mass ratio between the planet and the Sun, the eccentricity and inclination of the planet's orbit, and the presence of other planets in the system. In general, Trojans are more stable around planets with low eccentricity and inclination, and in systems with few other planets.

Jupiter Trojans

The Jupiter Trojans are by far the most numerous group of Trojans in the Solar System. They are thought to number about the same as the asteroids of the asteroid belt. The first Jupiter Trojan to be discovered was 588 Achilles by Max Wolf in 1906. By convention, they are named after figures from the Trojan War. The objects located at the L4 Lagrange point are named after Greek figures, and are called the Greek camp; those at the L5 point are named after Trojan figures and are called the Trojan camp.

Neptune Trojans

Nine Neptune Trojans are currently known, 2005 TN53, 2007 VL82, 2006 RJ103, 2005 TO74, 2008 LC18, 2004 UP10, 2011 HM102, 2010 VZ98 and 2014 QR330. They are less stable than the Jupiter Trojans because Neptune's orbit is more eccentric and inclined than Jupiter's.

Mars Trojans

26 Mars Trojans are currently known. The first one discovered was 5261 Eureka in 1990.

Earth Trojans

Two Earth Trojans are currently known: 2010 TK7, which dynamically orbits the Sun but appears to loop around Earth (the motion is chaotic and not permanently bound to Earth); and (469219) 2016 HO3, which is a quasi-satellite of Earth, following a similar, but more stable, orbit.

Other Trojans

In addition to the Trojans of Jupiter, Neptune, Mars, and Earth, Trojans have also been discovered orbiting Saturn's moon Tethys (Telesto and Calypso), and Saturn's moon Dione (Helene and Polydeuces). These moons do not orbit a planet, but are locked into a 1:1 resonance with their host moons.

It has been suggested that the planet Venus may have Trojans. However, no Venus Trojans have been discovered to date. This may be because Venus' orbit is very close to the Sun, making it difficult to observe objects in that region of the sky.

Transient Trojans

Some objects may become transient Trojans for a period of time before being ejected from the Lagrange point. A number of asteroids and centaurs have been identified as transient Trojans of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.

In hierarchical triple star systems, one star may orbit the other two stars in a Trojan-like orbit.

A 2013 analysis of data from the Kepler space telescope suggested that planets in other star systems can have stable Trojans.

A 2023 study suggested that some hot Jupiters may have moons that are in Trojan orbits.

Trojan binaries

Binary systems are rare among Trojan asteroids. The Trojan asteroid (90) Antiope is a binary asteroid of two components of almost equal size. A few other Trojans are also known to be binaries, such as (617) Patroclus, (624) Hektor, and (19020) 2000 ET70.

Close encounters with other objects

Trojans are protected from close encounters with their host planet because they are in a 1:1 orbital resonance with it. However, Trojans can have close encounters with other objects in the Solar System, such as asteroids and comets. These close encounters can change the Trojan's orbit, and in some cases can even eject the Trojan from the Lagrange point.

Observational challenges

Trojans are difficult to observe because they are faint and located near the Sun. This makes it difficult to obtain accurate measurements of their orbits and physical properties. In addition, Trojans are often located in crowded regions of the sky, which makes it difficult to distinguish them from background stars.

reference: From 1851 and until 1973 Greenlandic was written in the alphabet invented by Samuel Kleinschmidt . This alphabet employed the special character kra ( Κʻ / ĸ ) which was replaced by q in the 1973 reform . In the Kleinschmidt alphabet , long vowels and geminate consonants were indicated by means of diacritics on the vowels ( in the case of consonant gemination , the diacritics were placed on the vowel preceding the affected consonant ) . For example , the name Kalaallit Nunaat was spelled Kalâdlit Nunât . This scheme uses a circumflex accent ( ˆ ) to indicate a long vowel ( e.g. , ât / ît / ût , modern : aat , iit , uut ) , an acute accent ( ´ ) to indicate gemination of the following consonant : ( i.e. , á , í , ú modern : a ( kk ) , i ( kk ) , u ( kk ) ) ] and , finally , a tilde ( ˜ ) or a grave accent ( ` ) , depending on the author , indicates vowel length and gemination of the following consonant ( e.g. , ãt , ĩt , ũt or àt , ìt , ùt , modern : aatt , iitt , uutt ) . The letters ê and ô , used only before r and q , are now written er / eq and or / oq in Greenlandic . The spelling system of Nunatsiavummiutut , spoken in Nunatsiavut in northeastern Labrador , is derived from the old Greenlandic system .

The German word for them is Meerschweinchen , literally " little sea pig " , which has been translated into Polish as świnka morska , into Hungarian as tengerimalac , and into Russian as морская свинка . This derives from the Middle High German name merswin . This originally meant " dolphin " and was used because of the animals ' grunting sounds ( which were thought to be similar ) . Many other , possibly less scientifically based explanations of the German name exist . For example , sailing ships stopping to reprovision in the New World would pick up stores of guinea pigs , which provided an easily transportable source of fresh meat . The French term is cochon d 'Inde ( Indian pig ) or cobaye ; the Dutch call it Guinees biggetje ( Guinean piglet ) or cavia ( while in some Dutch dialects it is called Spaanse rat ) ; and in Portuguese , the guinea pig is variously referred to as cobaia , from the Tupi word via its Latinization , or as porquinho da Índia ( little Indian pig ) . This is not universal ; for example , the common word in Spanish is conejillo de Indias ( little rabbit of the Indies ) . The Chinese refer to them as 豚鼠 ( túnshǔ , ' pig mouse ' ) , and sometimes as Netherlands pig ( 荷蘭豬 , hélánzhū ) or Indian mouse ( 天竺鼠 , tiānzhúshǔ ) . The Japanese word for guinea pig is " モルモット " ( morumotto ) , which derives from the name of another mountain @-@ dwelling rodent , the marmot ; this is what guinea pigs were called by the Dutch traders who first brought them to Nagasaki in 1843 .

A low level circulation center was noted by JTWC on December 19 at 0600 UTC . Two days later , convection consolidated near the circulation center , and JMA began tracking it at 0000 UTC as a tropical depression . JTWC issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert at 1500 UTC , as sea level pressure began to deepen , and signs of upper level divergence were found in the system . The first advisory for Tropical Depression 42W followed three hours later , on December 17 at 1200 UTC . JTWC upgraded the depression to a tropical storm on December 22 at 0000 UTC as it traveled westerly , and was given the name Fern . According to JTWC , the wind speeds meandered at minimal tropical storm strength . JMA proceeded to upgrade the depression into a tropical storm at 1800 UTC , with winds of 65 km / h ( 40 mph ) , and a pressure reading of 996 hectopascals ( 996 mbar ) . On Christmas Eve , Fern slowly traveled toward Yap . The storm passed over Yap the next day , strengthening to 105 km / h ( 65 mph ) at 0000 UTC , according to JTWC . reference: The 4 × 100 m medley relay was the focal point of Tonelli 's Moscow campaign . The event had always been won by the United States since its inception at the Olympics at the 1960 Games , and their boycott had opened up the field . Australia 's best result had come in the inaugural race , when it out @-@ touched Japan to claim silver . The only other time that it had won a medal was in 1964 , taking bronze , and the previous outing in 1976 had seen Australia eliminated in the heats . Australia was regarded as a chance of a medal , but were not seen as the main threats , with Sweden , Great Britain and the Soviet Union the most heavily fancied teams . The hosts ' team included the silver medallists in the 100 m backstroke and breaststroke , and their butterflyer had come fifth ; their freestyler would come fourth in his event . The British boasted Duncan Goodhew , the breaststroke gold medallist , while Sweden 's butterflyer and backstroker had won their respective events and their freestyle swimmer would come second in the 100 m . On paper , Australia 's team paled in comparison . Neil Brooks , the freestyler , would come fourteenth in the corresponding individual event after having an asthma attack , while Peter Evans was the only individual medallist in the distance , claiming bronze in the 100 m breaststroke . Kerry had been eliminated in the backstroke semifinals , while Tonelli was swimming as a makeshift butterflyer . Adding to the pressure was the fact that Australia won no gold medals at the 1976 Olympics in any sport , so the public were still awaiting their first victory since the 1972 Games in Munich . Jan Hus (c. 1369 – 6 July 1415), also known as John Huss, was a Czech theologian, philosopher, master, reformer, and priest. Hus is considered the first Church reformer after John Wycliffe because he lived before Martin Luther, John Calvin and Huldrych Zwingli.

Hus was a key predecessor to the Protestant movement of the sixteenth century, and his continued defiance of the Church of Rome led to his excommunication and condemnation for heresy by the Council of Constance. He was burned at the stake on 6 July 1415.

Hus was born in Husinec, Bohemia (present-day Czech Republic).
Hus became a priest in 1400, and a professor and rector at the Charles University in Prague.

Jan Hus promoted Wycliffe’s reforms, which resulted in him being condemned by the Roman Catholic Church. Hus was a strong advocate for Czech autonomy and nationalism, and he was against German influence in Bohemia. Hus was also a major influence on the religious life of Bohemia.

reference: Prithvi Kumar Agrawala has traced at least six different lists of fifty or more aspects or forms of Ganesha each with their specific female consorts or shaktis . In these lists of paired shaktis are found such goddess names as Hrī , Śrī , Puṣṭī , etc . The names Buddhi , Siddhi , and Riddhi do not appear on any of these lists . The lists provide no details about the personalities or distinguishing iconographic forms for these shaktis . Agrawala concludes that all of the lists were derived from one original set of names . The earliest of the lists appears in the Nārada Purāṇa ( I.66.124 @-@ 38 ) , and appears to have been used with minor variations in the Ucchiṣṭagaṇapati Upāsanā . These lists are of two types . In the first type the names of various forms of Ganesha are given with a clear @-@ cut pairing of a named shakti for that form . The second type , as found in the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa ( II.IV.44.63 – 76 ) and the commentary of Rāghavabhaṭṭa on the Śāradātilaka ( I.115 ) , gives fifty or more names of Ganesha collectively in one group , with the names of the shaktis provided collectively in a second group . The second type of list poses problems in separating and properly connecting the names into pairs due to ambiguities in the formation of Sanskrit compound words .

The _History of the Han_ lists him as a son of Prince Jing of Zhongshan, Liu Sheng. His mother, Lady Zhao, was one of Liu Sheng's many consorts. Liu Bei claimed descent from Liu Sheng, but his exact ancestry is ambiguous as Liu Sheng reputedly had over 120 sons.

Liu Bei initially served as a minor government official commanding a unit of volunteers that suppressed the Yellow Turban Rebellion in the late Eastern Han dynasty. In 194, he defended Xu province from an invasion by Cao Cao, who was avenging his father's murder by a subordinate of Xu province's governor, Tao Qian. As Tao Qian was dying later that year, he bequeathed Xu province to Liu Bei.

In 196, Liu Bei sheltered Lü Bu, who had been defeated by Cao Cao, in Xu province. Lü Bu betrayed Liu Bei by seizing control of Xu province from him. Liu Bei joined Cao Cao to defeat Lü Bu at the Battle of Xiapi in 198. Liu Bei then followed Cao Cao back to the imperial capital, Xu, where Emperor Xian honoured him as "Uncle of the Emperor".

reference: As the first four matches of the series were drawn , the final Test , played at The Oval , was decisive . Aware that England had beaten Australia only once in 19 matches , the selectors made several changes to the team ; Chapman , at the time fourth in the national batting averages , replaced Carr as captain . This decision was controversial ; the press favoured Carr , particularly as Chapman was young , unproven as captain and not fully established in the team . When the match began on 14 August , Chapman won the toss and decided that England should bat first . When it was his turn to bat , he was given a good reception by the crowd . During his innings , Wisden noted , Chapman " hit out in vigorous fashion " , but once he was dismissed for 49 , the remaining batsmen were out quickly , leaving England with a disappointing total of 280 . Australia replied with 302 . On a pitch affected by rain , England then scored 436 , mainly because of a large partnership between opening batsmen Jack Hobbs and Herbert Sutcliffe . Australia needed to score 415 to win , which was unlikely given the condition of the pitch . The team were bowled out for 125 , and at least one of Chapman 's tactical decisions resulted in Australia losing a wicket . Wisden reported that " not a catch was missed nor was a run given away , the whole England side rising gallantly to the occasion . Naturally a scene of tremendous enthusiasm occurred at the end , the crowd swarming in thousands in front of the pavilion , and loudly cheering the players , both English and Australian . " The correspondent also commented " Chapman ... despite lack of experience in leading a first @-@ class team in the field , turned out a very happy nomination for the post of captain , the young amateur , for the most part , managing his bowling with excellent judgement , and in two or three things he did , showing distinct imagination . " Throughout the match , Chapman chose to follow his own tactics rather than rely on the veteran players in the team for advice . In the series , he scored 175 runs at 58 @.@ 33 .
